gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-new-tegomin: New Tegomin has a dignified, traditional look, its c opening like a wide ring on the page. And Red Hat Display sits over it with a marker-like line, bold and modern, with the same stroke width throughout.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-serif-hk: Noto Serif HK reads editorial and dignified, with crossbars a touch thinner than its stems and generous gaps where curves end. Yet Red Hat Display above it keeps every stroke uniform, so a bold, tubelike heading leads into a softly shaded serif.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-serif-jp: Refined and literary, Noto Serif JP draws a text serif line that feels steady but faintly modulated, with an unclenched c. But Red Hat Display, with its identical bar thickness, earns its keep when set big and short.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-serif-kr: Noto Serif KR is a refined text serif with wide s curves, barely curled in, and mild thick-thin shifts that smooth the reading pace. Noto Serif KR carries a hint of pen pressure in each curve, while Red Hat Display above it stays tube-like and constant in width.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-serif-sc: Rounded, see-through and refined, Noto Serif SC thickens only slightly at its sides, under a heading pulled like solder through a nozzle. Make Red Hat Display small and that bold, uniform stroke loses its punch.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-serif-tc: Marker-bold up top, quietly traditional below. Noto Serif TC holds its letters open with stems only a shade heavier than their arms, while Red Hat Display, with no swelling in its bowls, does the loud work.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-petrona: Red Hat Display holds one steady pen pressure from first letter to last. Petrona is the dignified, editorial partner, its diagonals slightly lighter than its verticals, a tempered serif that carries the text while the heading makes the statement.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-podkova: Red Hat Display draws a constant-width outline you could follow with a finger, bold and contemporary. And Podkova, a bookish, traditional serif with a broad, welcoming c, settles into a long read with an easy, familiar pace.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-poly: Strokes like laser-cut sheet, all one width, give Red Hat Display its contemporary bite. Then Poly, a bookish text serif with bowls that thin slightly at the sides, adds a wedge-shaped pen softness underneath it.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-radley: Red Hat Display holds each stroke to one thickness like a drawn cable, leaving visible daylight in every curve. Radley, a classic serif, handles the reading with robust downstrokes and slender turns.
